Package com.github.tommyettinger.cringe

Class WangPerlueNoise

java.lang.Object
com.github.tommyettinger.cringe.RawNoise
com.github.tommyettinger.cringe.WangRawNoise
com.github.tommyettinger.cringe.WangPerlueNoise
All Implemented Interfaces:
com.badlogic.gdx.utils.Json.Serializable, Externalizable, Serializable
public class WangPerlueNoise extends WangRawNoise
Perlue Noise, adapted to use compatible edges for a Wang tiling or omni-tiling. Perlue is a mix of "Classic" Perlin noise, written by Ken Perlin before he created Simplex Noise, with value noise calculated at the same time. This should be used with WangContinuousNoise, not the regular ContinuousNoise. This only creates tiling areas that are squares, cubes, or hypercubes; it can't make other tiling shapes.
You can request a set of 16 2D Wang tiles by giving this 16 sequential seeds and filling the WangContinuousNoise.getTileSize() with 2D noise. You can use 3D noise or higher dimensions for this case as well, as long as the extra dimensions aren't too close to 0 or the tile size (which would make them use the same pattern for every texture). Unlike most Wang-tiling solutions, you can also request Wang-tiling cubes, where the inside of each cube is very different but the faces are compatible with each other. You could even, for some reason, request Wang hypercubes up to 6D. That would need 4096 6D cubes, though.
An alternative is to use omni-tiling or single-edge mode, with WangContinuousNoise.setSingleEdge(boolean). You can request up to 16 omni-tiling squares that all have compatible edges if you use 2D, up to 64 omni-tiling cubes if you use 3D, and so on. You can also just get a 2D slice of the 3D cubes by using the same value for z in every call (again, not too close to 0 or tileSize).
Internally, this works by changing the seed to an alternate one when the noise is close to an edge. That makes the gradient/value used for edges at a specific position always the same (the alternate seed doesn't change), unless it's a Wang tile edge that should be different.

    • equalize

      public static float equalize(float x, float add, float mul)
      Given inputs as x in the range -1.0 to 1.0 that are too biased towards 0.0, this "squashes" the range softly to widen it and spread it away from 0.0 without increasing bias anywhere else.
      This starts with a common sigmoid function, x / sqrt(x * x + add), but instead of approaching -1 and 1 but never reaching them, this multiplies the result so the line crosses -1 when x is -1, and crosses 1 when x is 1. It has a smooth derivative, if that matters to you.
      Parameters:
      x - a float between -1 and 1
      add - if greater than 1, this will have nearly no effect; the lower this goes below 1, the more this will separate results near the center of the range. This must be greater than or equal to 0.0
      mul - typically the result of calling (float) Math.sqrt(add + 1f)
      Returns:
      a float with a slightly different distribution from x, but still between -1 and 1
